name: OGL
role: Tiny zero-dependency WebGL library with a Three.js-like API, about 29 KB
summary: Minimal ES-module WebGL library with Geometry, Program, Mesh, Camera, Transform, RenderTarget and a few extras, shaped like a lean Three.js. You write your own shaders and drive render calls from time. Output is a canvas. Distinguishing strength: very small, readable source with no dependencies.
use_when: Over Three.js for a single custom-shader mesh or fullscreen effect with minimal code
Over regl when a scene graph and camera classes help but Three.js is overkill
Tiny bundle for a self-contained generative scene
avoid_when: glTF, PBR, shadows or postprocessing: Three.js
Thin helpers over raw WebGL only: TWGL

evidence.result: 90 distinct 1280x720 alpha frames at 30 fps; all shuffled hashes equal sequential; frame 45 alpha min 0 max 1. Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Node 22.19.0; screenshot route. Contact sheet inspected.
evidence.scope: OGL Renderer (alpha, premultiplied), Camera, Transform, custom-shader Program, Box and Sphere; time uniform from t; no unseeded clocks. macOS arm64 Chromium 156 only; no export.

notes: 2026-10-26: npm metadata and README say Unlicense but the repository licence field is empty.

assessment.rationale: Last npm release Jan 2025 and last repo push Apr 2025, so 18 to 21 months idle: slow. Small, dependency-free, public-domain, and stable for custom-shader work.
